newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Caribbean nations pledge to help Montserrat.
newsitem.headline: Caribbean nations pledge to help Montserrat.

text.p: The 15-member Caribbean Community (Caricom) on Friday pledged to assist the island of Montserrat as it attempts to recover from last week's volcanic eruptions, but said assistance from Britain for its colony had been lagging.
The major eruption on June 25 left at least nine people dead and destroyed nine communities and 200 homes.

Montserrat is the only Caricom member that is not an independent state. Since the volcanic activity started in July 1995, more than a third of the island's approximately 12,000 inhabitants have left, and another 1,250 live in shelters on the island.

Just over 1,200 have taken up a British offer that provides them with housing and a weekly allowance, provided they pay their airfare to the U.K. Antiguan officials say they have over 3,000 Montserratians living in shelters there with more arriving daily, and smaller numbers are now in the British Virgin Islands, St. Kitts and Dominica.

Montserrat's Education Minister Adelina Tuitt, who heads the delegation to the Caricom summit being held in Jamaica, said her government had so far spent some 3.5 million pounds sterling ($6 million) from the 25 million pounds ($42.2 million) allocated by London for emergency relief.

She said further spending for the most pressing issues, such as housing and infrastructure, has been hindered by London's insistence that the government must first submit project proposals before more funds can be released.
Tuitt said that due to diplomatic and bureaucratic hurdles, Montserrat had not been getting funds from Britain "as quickly as we would like it."

Caricom members pledged to help Montserrat develop the necessary formal requests to Britain for more funding, and a number of states offered to take small numbers of Montserratian children now living in shelters.
